title: Run Here, Ship There: Which Binaries Run During the Build, Which Go to the Robot, and the Bug a Native Build Hides

questions.question: Why does a native build pass a graph with a generator built for the target?
options: The compiler notices and builds the generator for the host
It does not pass: the graph has 4 problems either way
A native build never runs the generator
The target is the host, so it runs: every mistake about which machine is invisible
questions.explanation: When the laptop is also the target, a program built for the target runs on the laptop. The same graph had 0 problems native and 4 when built for the robot.

questions.question: Which machine must a code generator that the build runs be built for?
options: The target, like every other executable
The host, or a target the host could run
Either: the build picks whichever exists
Neither: generators are scripts
questions.explanation: The build executes it, so it has to run where the build runs. An aarch64 generator cannot be executed on an x86_64 laptop.

questions.question: A robot program links a library that was built on the laptop. What goes wrong?
options: The library is the wrong architecture for the robot, and it fails to link or to load
Nothing: a library is only data until it is loaded
It links, and runs more slowly
It links, and is larger than it need be
questions.explanation: The library's code is for the laptop's processor. The robot's linker refuses it, or the robot cannot load it.

questions.question: Is a host tool in the bundle an error the compiler reports?
options: Yes: the linker refuses a host binary
No: it builds fine and the robot is shipped with a binary it cannot run
Yes, as a warning
Only if the tool is larger than the bundle allows
questions.explanation: Nothing in the build objects to installing a file. The robot ends up carrying a tool it cannot run, and only a check of the graph says so.

questions.question: What does the fix cost?
options: Nothing: the fixed graph is strictly better
A slower robot
Some tests no longer run in the build, and a library may be built twice, once for each machine
A second sysroot
questions.explanation: Tests built for the robot cannot run during the build, and a library both machines need is compiled twice. Two machines are two builds.

questions.question: What is the real check of all this?
options: A native build that passes
A unit test of the graph checker
A cross build in continuous integration, which this repository does not have
A review of the build files
questions.explanation: The checker models the rules. A real cross build is what shows whether the project obeys them, and this repository's CI does not have one.
